title: Disgust sensitivity predicts intuitive disapproval of gays
central_claims: Disgust sensitivity predicts intuitive disapproval of gay people, via differential intentionality judgments and implicit associations.

source_manifest.title: Many Labs2: Investigating Variation in Replicability Across Samples and Settings
source_manifest.finding: The specific disgust-by-gay-kissing contrast shrank from q=.70 to q=.05; the authors considered the overall result inconsistent with the original differential association. Disgust and intentionality correlations themselves remained weakly positive.

source_manifest.title: Sensitivity to disgust,but not increased disgust,is associated with disapproval of gays: Experimental evidence from Turkey
source_manifest.finding: Study2finds a dispositional disgust/negative-attitudes correlation; manipulated disgust has no reliable effect. This is partial conceptual support,not the original implicit-intentionality interaction.

research.summary: The specific disgust-by-gay-kissing contrast shrank from q=.70 to q=.05; the authors considered the overall result inconsistent with the original differential association. Disgust and intentionality correlations themselves remained weakly positive. Wider adoption and practical utility are not inferred from replication. A2024Turkish extension gives partial dispositional support but no causal disgust effect; overall evidence is mixed.
